title: Hackett friendship: Condon's Tuesday sessions and Jackie Gleason parties
summary: Leeman sorts out dates, saying Hackett did not hire him until 1949-50, and recalls Condon's jam sessions, Gleason's private parties and Whiteman radio dates.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: I misplaced ten easy years, Bobby didn't take me

and I was out with the big bands, and when I returned to New York, Bobby didn't take me into Nicks in the Village, which had then moved over to 10th Street and 7th Avenue, he didn't take me in there until '49 and the first of '50. Not '39-'40.

If this is confusing to you, you're right. It's also confusing me, but I have to get my dates straightened out here. After that, we used to have Tuesday night jam sessions at Eddie Condon's, and that was one of the features of the club, and Lips Page used to be one of his regulars, and Bobby Hackett, too. So we kept in touch. Bobby Hackett used to play there every once in awhile, and he was great.

We played a good many private parties for Jackie Gleason. Jackie Gleason just loved Bobby Hackett, and we used to play quite a few of those at Toots Shoor's. Bobby was always a regular at the Gibson parties, and we kept in constant contact. We did lots of record dates together. Bobby worked at the time in that era, he worked at ABC Radio and TV. He also worked with the Whiteman group -- Whiteman kept the radio band at ABC, a couple of times a week.

And Bobby would ask me to be on the programs a couple of times -- Paul Whiteman had Jack Teagarden back with Bobby Hackett, and he loved it. And Bobby would always ask for me to play drums; he didn't care for the staff drummer behind him, and so we had some pleasant moments then.
